calls.head: The Blackhawks will send Cole and Vlasic at Rantanen
calls.body: At home, the Blackhawks keep sending Cole and Vlasic out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jeff Blashill has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Stars’ first line is Rantanen, Hintz and Robertson.

calls.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
calls.body: On the power play, Dallas is one of the league’s best, but Chicago is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Blackhawks take could cost them.

surprises.head: A shutout for Jake Oettinger
surprises.body: Oettinger stopped all 19 shots, worth 2.8 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 50 starts.

surprises.head: Chicago found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Chicago usually gets worse looks than most teams. Not tonight: an 8.8% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.1% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: Oettinger blanks the Blackhawks
paras: The first goal of the game would have been Dallas’, but it was taken off for offside midway through the first. They got it back early in the second, when Jason Robertson officially opened the scoring on the power play. Arttu Hyry made it 2-0 late in the period, and he scored his second of the night early in the third to make it 3-0. Roope Hintz made it 4-0 midway through the period.
The Stars had the better of the chances, outshooting the Blackhawks 32-19. Jake Oettinger was perfect for the Stars, 19 saves on 19 shots, and Spencer Knight stopped 28 of 32.
The Stars killed all four Blackhawks power plays. The Stars improved to 4-3-1, and the Blackhawks dropped to 3-6-0.

items.text: Connor Bedard’s seven-game point streak against Dallas ended.
